Cached under itemtext/.cache/silva_2022_crsy/.
note: Written, clean gate pass (batch_390): 80 rows = 16 items x resp 1-5; validate_items.R --table-sets PASS (16/16 items, resp 1-5). CODE DERIVATION: data/silva_2022_crsy.py builds crsy_NN from the leading questionnaire number in each column's SPSS variable LABEL ('7. There is a lot of help...' -> crsy_07), not from the column name, because the .sav's names were renumbered after the four validation deletions (Res_6 is questionnaire item 7, Res_10 is item 14; deleted items are Res_6_deleted/Res_11_deleted/Res_12_deleted/Res_13_deleted = items 6/11/12/13). Not positional: the code is read off the label that carries the text, so item_text and item come from the same string. REPRODUCED: re-parsed the .sav and compared per-column level counts with the live table: all 16 x 5 = 80 item-by-level counts match exactly (e.g. crsy_06 = Res_6_deleted 652/1090/1337/369/115; crsy_07 = Res_6 244/677/1501/840/301; crsy_16 = Res_12 1682/611/710/366/194), n=3563 per item. Paper corroboration: the Results paragraph quotes deleted items by the same numbers as the labels (item 6 'In my region there are many job opportunities', 11, 12, 13), and Table 2's retained items 1-12 are labels 1-5, 7-10, 14-16 in order; the Zenodo scoring guide (Factor 1 = items 1-5, 2 = 6-9, 3 = 10-12 in retained numbering) and the .sav's Res_Factor labels ('Compute 7,8,9,10'; '14,15, 16') agree. TEXT: item_text is the .sav label verbatim with its leading 'N. ' numbering stripped; label 11 has no final period and ships without one. The .sav uses American 'organize/organized' (items 2, 3, 14, 16) and 'Communities' capitalised in item 14, where the paper's Table 2 prints 'organise/organised' and 'communities'; the data file is level 1, so its spelling ships. LANGUAGE: administered to 3,563 students in Portuguese schools in 2017-2018; the administered language is not stated but is inferred as Portuguese (Portuguese secondary schools, MoE/MIME-approved questionnaire; the deposit file is suffixed _eng). Checked for Portuguese wording: the deposit's only file (the _eng .sav: all labels English), the paper full text, and S1 File (pone.0269027.s001.docx, the response-to-reviewers letter) - no item wording in Portuguese in any, so text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied (the authors' own English in their data file and paper). OPTIONS: value labels are bare '1'..'5' and the paper prints no anchors, so option_text is blank for all levels (not padded). The Zenodo record's scoring guide describes the scale as '5-point Likert scale (1=low agreement to 5=high agreement)'; that is a description for data users, not the printed anchor wording, so it is not shipped as option_text. instructions blank: no participant instructions published. One trivial section_id. INSTRUMENT (Step 3b): matches - the paper's own new 16-item pool, 12 retained; itemcov_retained in the response table marks the 12. RIGHTS: the CRS-Y is this study's own instrument, published in a CC BY 4.0 article and CC BY 4.0 deposit; no instrument_rights_register.csv row; no restriction located to quote; silence = permission, no register row written.
public_note: Item text is the English wording in the authors' own data file; the survey of Portuguese students was presumably administered in Portuguese, and that version was not published.

note: mapping_basis=data_labels: item codes ARE the source column names lowercased by the .do (rename *, lower) -- no positional step. 3563.sav VARIABLE labels tie each column to its text: P1 "Grado de preocupación por la existencia en España de noticias falsas y/o la divulgación de bulos" (a summary; the shipped item_text is the full P.1 question from cues3563.pdf), DESINFOR_1..4 "Manipular la opinión pública" / "Erosionar la estabilidad de los Estados y sus instituciones" / "Generar conflictos de convivencia en la sociedad" / "Crear polarización política", P12_1..5 "La protección de la salud" / "La convivencia pacífica en la sociedad" / "El medio ambiente" / "La seguridad de los/as ciudadanos/as" / "La democracia" -- 9/9 battery labels identical to the questionnaire rows in the same order. VALUE labels on all 10: 1 Mucho, 2 Bastante, 3 Poco, 4 Nada, 8 N.S., 9 N.C.; the .do drops 8/9. Cross-check: the live table per-item x resp counts match the .sav frequencies cell for cell, 40/40 (e.g. p1 1711/1161/421/169, desinfor_1 1977/1191/236/69, p12_3 1026/1189/962/263), N=3492 ids. Rights: CIS own questionnaire, not a third-party instrument; CIS reuse conditions permit reuse with attribution, same basis as the shipped spain_2025_*/spain_2026_* CIS tables. Dictionary defect: the IRW dictionary Reference for this table names "Índice de Confianza del Consumidor. Mes de mayo 2026, Estudio 3565", but the data URL, the .do input (3563_num.csv) and the item content are Estudio 3563 "Desinformación y humor"; the Reference should be corrected.

CHECKED ANYWAY, decisively: re-running the .do logic on 3563_num.csv (N=3493; id = row number; 8/9 to missing; no recode) reproduces the live table exactly -- 13726 rows, id-item-resp row sets identical (0/0 set differences) against the local irw cache copy written by table_context.R (no additional export). TEXT: text_source=study_materials, Spanish transcribed from cues3563.pdf (pdftotext -layout and -raw agree). instructions = the P.10 question verbatim with the interviewer direction '(ENTREVISTADOR/A: LEER UNA A UNA Y MARCAR RESPUESTA).' dropped (not addressed to the respondent). item_text = the grid row labels; p10_4 wraps across two lines in the PDF and is joined with a space. ONE WORDING DIFFERENCE: the questionnaire prints p10_4 as '...piensan políticamente diferente a nosotros/as' while the .sav/ES3563/codigo labels read 'diferentes'; the shipped item_text follows the questionnaire (what was read aloud), the other 3 items agree with the labels character for character. option_text = the grid column headers, identical to the value labels. No CATI fill tokens; no filter precedes P.10 (asked of all). section_prompt blank, single trivial section_id. RESP: CIS codes 1..4 stored unchanged; resp 1 = Mucho (contributes most) ... 4 = Nada. All four levels used on every item; every item has four option rows; 8/9 have no option row. translation_source=machine_translation: CIS publishes Estudio 3563 in Spanish only; the four _translated columns were written by IRW.
